report:
# Report: `region.fasta` (`region_004`, 3000 bp)

**File facts:** one FASTA record, 3000 bp, plain ACGT. A 23.2 / C 23.6 / G 28.4 / T 24.7 %, GC 52.1 %, GC skew +0.048. CpG observed/expected = 1.22, so this is *not* CpG-suppressed DNA (i.e. not vertebrate).

## The one thing that stands out: a ~900-codon ORF with textbook bacterial start signals

| Feature | Coordinates (1-based) |
|---|---|
| In-frame stop that closes the upstream frame | `TGA` 113–115 |
| Shine–Dalgarno-like `GGAGG` | 145–149 |
| Spacer | 150–157 (8 nt — optimal SD spacing) |
| Start codon `ATG` | 158–160 |
| CDS | 158–2851 (898 codons → 898 aa protein) |
| Stop codon `TAA` | 2852–2854 |

The reading frame (+2) is open from 116 all the way to 2851 — a stop‑free stretch of 2,736 nt, which by chance is essentially impossible. The ATG at 158 is the *first* in‑frame ATG anywhere in this frame. Protein begins `MFKEIFTRLIRHLPSRLVHRDPLPGAQQ…` and ends `…SYFPWLVAILAGYMTLTQLVKGFYSRRYGWQ`; it contains 29 internal Met codons. The other five frames contain nothing longer than 206 aa, and that one (minus strand, 1737–2352) lies entirely inside the gene.

## But the CDS looks engineered rather than naturally evolved

The reading frame is conspicuously depleted of certain codons, while the *same* triplets are abundant at non‑coding positions in the same 3 kb — so this is a frame-specific effect, not a genome-wide compositional bias:

| codon | in the 898‑codon ORF | expected | count at non‑ORF positions (~2100 codons) |
|---|---|---|---|
| AGA | 0 | 13.8 | 31 |
| AGG | 0 | 16.9 | 34 |
| CGA | 0 | 14.0 | 49 |
| ATA | 1 | 12.0 | 34 |
| CTA | 3 | 12.2 | 11 |

Zero of ~45 expected "A‑ending" Arg codons is ~1e‑20 by chance. The pattern (CTG/GTG/GCG/CCG/CGC/CGT preferred, AGA/AGG/CGA/ATA/CTA avoided) is exactly what you get from back‑translating a protein with an *E. coli*-style preferred‑codon table. The protein's amino‑acid composition is also atypical (χ² = 51, df 19): enriched in Ala/Leu/Ile/Val/Met/Trp/Thr, depleted in Lys, Tyr, Cys, Asn.

## Nothing else found

- No tandem repeats, no exactly repeated 12‑mer, longest inverted repeat only 11 bp; no CRISPR array, no common restriction sites, longest homopolymer 5 nt (T171–175, A1470–1475).
- The protein contains no recognisable catalytic signature from a motif scan (no P‑loop/Walker A, no Rossmann, no HEXXH, no C2H2/RING, no aaRS HIGH/KMSKS), no signal peptide, and only one modest hydrophobic stretch (aa 100–125); it looks largely helical/solenoid-like, but I can't assign a function.
- No rho‑independent terminator in the 146 nt downstream (longest T‑run is TTTT at 2904–2907); with only 157 nt upstream, no promoter is identifiable either.

## Bottom line

The only notable, confidently assignable feature is the single large ORF (158–2854, 898 aa) with a Shine–Dalgarno/start/stop architecture. Two caveats: (1) I have no database access, so I cannot give a function — that needs a BLAST/HMM search against UniProt/RefSeq; (2) the frame-specific codon depletion and odd amino-acid composition mean I would not treat this as a wild-type genomic gene until it's checked against a real sequence database — it may be a synthetic or back-translated construct.

(A copy of this summary is saved as `scratch/report.md`.)
